title: Philippines, Japan vow to deepen strategic partnership

blocks.text: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi hold bilateral talks at the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC) in Pasay City on November 16, 2026
PPA Pool photos by Niño Jesus Orbeta

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos met with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi yesterday on the sidelines of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Summits where they reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen the two countries’ strategic partnership.
Takaichi met with Marcos at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City, hours after arriving in Manila.
During the meeting, Marcos thanked the Japanese leader for participating in the ASEAN Summit here.
“I remember with great pleasure our karaoke session…over dinner in our last meeting,” Marcos told Takaichi, drawing laughter from Philippine and Japanese officials in attendance.
Marcos also cited significant progress in advancing relations between Manila and Tokyo.
Takaichi, for her part, said she is looking forward to further deepening ties with Manila.

“Based on our comprehensive strategic partnership between Japan and the Philippines, I look forward to further strengthening our bilateral relations through our meeting after this,” she said, as translated in English.
Takaichi will participate in the ASEAN Summit as dialogue partner of the regional bloc.
She will also co-chair the 4th Asia Zero Emission Community Leaders’ Meeting scheduled tomorrow.
AZEC is a Japan-led initiative aimed at promoting clean energy, reducing carbon emissions and supporting sustainable economic growth while strengthening energy security across the region.
The two leaders met in May during Marcos’ state visit to Japan, when the two countries elevated their relations to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

In October, the two leaders also held a telephone conversation, where they discussed various areas of cooperation, such as on the Luzon Economic Corridor, defense and security and Japan’s long-standing support to peace consolidation efforts in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region of Muslim Mindanao.
